sections.title: What RAG does for models

paragraphs.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation combines a retriever that finds relevant documents with a generator that answers using that context. This architecture addresses two fundamental limits: knowledge cutoff and hallucination.
paragraphs.explainArabic: RAG يجمع بين مسترجع يجد المستندات ذات الصلة ومشفر يجيب باستخدام هذا السياق. هذا يتجاوز قصور المعرفة والتوهم.

paragraphs.text: The retriever encodes queries and documents into a shared vector space, retrieves the most similar chunks, and feeds them to a language model that generates answers grounded in retrieved evidence.
paragraphs.explainArabic: المسترجع يرمز الأسئلة والمستندات في فضاء متجه مشترك، يسترجع القطع الأكثر تشابهًا ويغذيها لنموذج يجيب بناءً على الأدلة المسترجعة.

items: Document storage: Knowledge is chunked and embedded into a vector database.
Retrieval: Encode queries, find similar chunks, return top-K results.
Generation: Combine query plus retrieved context, let the model generate.

keySentences: RAG combines retrieval with generation for grounded answers.
The retriever and generator work together to answer questions.
takeaways: Retrieval finds relevant context from a knowledge base.
Generation uses that context to produce answers.
This architecture limits hallucinations by grounding responses.

studyAid.whyItMatters: RAG enables LLMs to answer questions about private data without retraining.

confusion.simpleEnglish: The model knows what it retrieved, not what's in training.
confusion.simpleArabic: الموديل يعرف ما استرجعه، ليس ما في التدريب.
confusion.analogy: A librarian who answers from retrieved books, not memory.

prediction.question: Why not just fine-tune on your data?
prediction.answer: Fine-tuning changes the model itself. RAG updates the knowledge base, which is easier and cheaper to maintain.

sections.title: Chunking affects retrieval quality

paragraphs.text: Documents must be chunked before embedding. Too large and chunks are too noisy; too small and concepts split across pieces.
paragraphs.explainArabic: المستندات يجب تقسيمها قبل التضمين. كبيرة جدًا تصبح ضوضاء، صغيرة جدًا تنقسم المفاهيم.

paragraphs.text: Compare retrieval with different chunk sizes:
paragraphs.code:
# Small chunks fit budget but may split concepts
small_chunks = document.split("\n\n", 10)  # by paragraphs
# Large chunks capture context but exceed token limits
large_chunks = create_sliding_windows(document, size=2048)

symbols.meaning: Context window available for the generator

keySentences: Chunk size balances precision with budget.
Concepts must stay within a single chunk.
takeaways: Larger chunks capture more context but cost more.
Smaller chunks fit budgets but may miss relationships.
Hierarchical chunking retrieves coarse, then refines.

studyAid.whyItMatters: Chunking strategy determines whether retrieval finds the right pieces of information.

confusion.simpleEnglish: Split a paragraph in half? The model loses both parts.
confusion.simpleArabic: قسم فقرة نصفين؟ الموديل يخسر كلا الجزأين.
confusion.analogy: Reading only one half of a sentence confuses the meaning.

prediction.question: Your retrieval returns 4 chunks but none mention 'price'. What's wrong?
prediction.answer: The query and chunks are too distant in vector space, or chunking broke up related content.

labs.title: RAG budget planner
labs.goal: Watch how chunk size and top-K affect the retrieved token total.

tasks.prompt: Set chunk size to 400 and top-K to 4. Read the retrieved token total.
tasks.check: Retrieved tokens equal chunk size times top-K (1600).

tasks.prompt: Raise chunk size to 800 and keep top-K at 4.
tasks.check: Retrieved tokens double (3200) and may exceed a 4096 token budget.

tasks.prompt: Lower chunk size to 200 and raise top-K to 8.
tasks.check: Retrieved tokens stay inside the budget while coverage grows.

labs.takeawayEn: Chunk size and retrieval count jointly determine the context bill.
labs.takeawayAr: حجم القطع وعدد المسترجعة يحددان معًا فاتورة السياق.
labs.simulationNote: Illustrative simulation, not real model output.

quiz.prompt: Why use RAG instead of fine-tuning?
options: RAG updates knowledge without changing the model weights.
Fine-tuning is cheaper than embedding a vector database.
The retriever generates answers directly, no model needed.
answer: RAG updates knowledge without changing the model weights.
quiz.explanationEn: RAG adds new knowledge to the knowledge base; fine-tuning changes model parameters.
quiz.explanationAr: RAG يضيف معرفة جديدة للأساس؛ التدريب يغير المعاملات.

quiz.explanationEn: Too large and chunks contain irrelevant information; too small and concepts split.
quiz.explanationAr: كبيرة جدًا تتخلل معلومات غير ذات صلة؛ صغيرة جدًا تنقسم المفاهيم.
